learning_objective: 🎯 Master the words that 'fix' nouns (Determiners) and the special helping verbs that express moods, attitudes, possibility, and obligation (Modals).

main_concepts.simple_explanation:
Determiners come before a noun. 
1. Articles: 'A/An' (General, singular) and 'The' (Specific, unique). 
2. Demonstratives: This, That, These, Those. 
3. Quantifiers: 'Some' (positive sentences/requests), 'Any' (negative/questions), 'Much' (uncountable nouns like water/money), 'Many' (countable nouns like books/boys).

Modals are helping verbs that never change form. 
• 'Can' shows present ability (I can swim) and informal permission. 
• 'Could' shows past ability (I could swim when I was 5) and polite request. 
• 'May' shows formal permission (May I come in?) and high possibility (It may rain today). 
• 'Might' shows very low possibility (It might rain, but the sky is clear).

• 'Must' shows strong obligation, strict rule, or necessity (You must wear a helmet). 
• 'Should' shows general advice or duty (You should respect elders). 
• 'Ought to' is similar to should, but indicates moral duty (We ought to love our country).

• 'Will / Shall': Indicates future. 'Shall' is used with I/We. 
• 'Would': Used for polite offers (Would you like some tea?) and past habits. 
• 'Used to': Also shows past habits that are now stopped (I used to play cricket).

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The 'Must' vs 'Should' Scale
fun_activity.instructions: 'Should' is a suggestion (Doctor says: You SHOULD eat apples). But 'Must' is an order/law! (Police says: You MUST stop at the red light). Try replacing 'must' with 'should' in the traffic rule—chaos! Modals change the entire severity of a sentence!

exam_tips: 📌 Modals are ALWAYS followed by the base form of the verb (V1). Never use V2, V3, or V-ing directly after a modal! (Correct: He can *go*. | Incorrect: He can *goes* / *went*).
📌 'Little / A little / The little' are used for UNCOUNTABLE nouns (Milk, Time, Money). 'Few / A few / The few' are used for COUNTABLE nouns (Boys, Books, Days).
📌 Sound matters for A/An! Use 'An' before vowel SOUNDS (अ, आ, इ, ई...), not just letters. e.g., 'An hour', 'An MP', 'A European', but 'A university', 'A one-eyed man'.
quick_recap: ⭐ Determiners 'fix' the noun, meaning a noun MUST follow them immediately.
⭐ 'Needn't' (Need not) and 'Daren't' (Dare not) act as semi-modals in negative and interrogative sentences.
⭐ 'Ought' and 'Used' are the only two modals that are always followed by the infinitive 'to'.
